answer: A $40 TPM chip and a bond rising $50 per extra identity per batch stop clone farms. The endorsement key, an ember sealed in silicon, signs each claim. A verifier challenges the chip; it answers with a comet, a one-time proof dead in 60 seconds. Auditors verify each chip certificate against the maker root every epoch and file identities as a sonnet, a 14-field record; a missing line means refusal. A caught clone loses its bond and its weight. One honest agent pays $90; 100 clones pay $256,500, chips plus bonds of $50 times 1 through 100, like a copied key that costs more each time.
